headline: High: open-webui’s broad networked, persistent web-app defaults can leak or misroute marker outputs, while marker’s local-only profile limits direct injection but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem, network, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest open-webui output by default. Open-webui can expose documents through persistent web-app sessions and MCP/tooling, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. The main pathway is manual or orchestrated copy-paste, so risk is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies open-webui output into marker inputs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or file-drop workflow.
Review copied text before feeding it into marker.
Use a one-way export format with no instructions preserved.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open-webui touches documents, files, notes, API keys, and persistent memory, and it can use mounted volumes plus broad network egress. Marker is local-only and does not read or write filesystems, so it is less likely to leak directly, but open-webui can still expose sensitive content through its web UI or external APIs in default deployments.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to a mounted volume containing sensitive documents, those contents may be exposed in its outputs.
IF open-webui is configured to send prompts or artifacts to third-party APIs, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any mounted volume.
Disable external API connectors for sensitive runs.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive workspace.
Rotate any API keys already loaded into open-webui.
Set retention to the shortest available window.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it has no meaningful write conflict with open-webui. Open-webui can write to local files or mounted volumes and supports persistent shared sessions, but the pair does not share overlapping write authority in the profiles. Conflict risk is therefore small.
conditions: IF marker is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access, write conflicts could emerge.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable mounted volume, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Do not mount the same writable directory into both agents.
Use separate output folders per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent and may produce extracted text that open-webui can ingest through files, prompts, or tools. Open-webui has broad tool and API surfaces, so if it treats marker output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or summaries. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF open-webui consumes marker output without a verification step, hallucinations or extraction errors can propagate.
IF open-webui uses marker output to drive tool calls or user-facing decisions, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add a human review step before actioning outputs.
Require source-link or quote verification in open-webui.
Mark marker output as untrusted metadata.
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text.

E_compliance.rationale: Open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, usage analytics, and persistent memory, while marker’s profile is sparse and does not document comparable retention or residency controls. Because the pair can move sensitive documents into a broader web-app environment, compliance gaps are plausible, but the evidence does not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through open-webui, retention and logging policies must be aligned.
IF open-webui stores prompts or artifacts longer than marker’s workflow expects, subject-rights handling may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in open-webui.
Disable analytics and long-term memory where possible.
Document retention settings before use.
Purge stored chats after each task.
Use separate instances for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
